newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Japan wants super power status. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China says Japan wants super power status. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: China said on Thursday that Japan was "walking in the shadow of the United States" by building up it military muscle and seeking the status of a super power.
Japan was also trying to mask its own ambitions by accusing China of being a threat to the Asian-Pacific region, the official Xinhua news agency said in a signed commentary.
"It is obvious that Japan is building up its military power steadily while claiming verbally that is has no desire to become a military powerhouse," Xinhua said.
"It is not China but Japan that walks in the shadow of the United States and seeks the status of a 'super power'."
Xinhua quoted a report from the London Institute of Strategic Studies as saying that Japan's military expenditures were the third largest in the world in 1995.

The commentary also said the U.S.-Japan security declaration signed in April, which expanded the scope of cooperation from the security of Japan to safeguarding the Asian-Pacific region, was further evidence of Tokyo's intentions.
China and Japan have been at loggerheads over a group of East China Sea islands that both sides claim.
The islands, called the Daioyus in Chinese and Senkakus in Japanese, are also claimed by Taiwan.
Beijing has lashed out at Japan's biggest political party, the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), for its inclusion of Tokyo's claim to the islands in its election platform.

Beijing (Corrects from Tokyo) also has taken aim at Japanese prime minister and LDP leader Ryutaro Hashimoto for breaking a decade-long taboo on prime ministerial visits to Tokyo's Yasukuni shrine to Japan's war dead.

"Japan's aim in disseminating the 'China threat' is to divert the attention of the international community and lull the world into letting down its guard so as to quietly achieve its long-coveted goal of becoming a major political and military power," the commentary said.
